function: Joint frequency-channel and transmit-power allocation across 16 beams of a LEO multi-beam satellite, maximizing throughput, fairness, energy efficiency and interference suppression (pp. 7, 10)
system: Single LEO satellite at 500 km, 16 beams (45 dBi), 32-256 user terminals (15 dBi), 64-128 frequency channels, 100 MHz bandwidth, 10 GHz carrier (pp. 4, 10-11)
method: Attention-MO-PPO: multi-objective PPO reinforcement learning with spatial and temporal attention, adaptive Pareto reward weights, hybrid discrete-continuous actions; trained offline on the ground, on-board inference (pp. 7-9)
data_channel: Custom Python simulator: free-space path loss, log-normal shadowing, Rayleigh fading, interference-aware inter-beam factor; users placed uniformly at random in 16 beams (pp. 4-5, 10)
test_conditions: Scenarios vary users 32-256, interference level, traffic load 50-150 Mbps, shadowing 4-12 dB; the paper does not state training conditions or a train/test split (pp. 10-11)
baselines: Non-learned: Proportional Fair and Max C/I; learned: MODRL-TF (multi-objective DRL) and basic PPO (p. 10)
metrics: System throughput, Jain fairness index, energy efficiency, interference suppression ratio, end-to-end delay, packet loss rate, inference time (pp. 11-14)
complexity: Inference O(N^2) in frequency channels versus O(N^3) for MODRL-TF; attention module O(L^2 d); measured inference 8.7 ms (96 users) and 22.3 ms (256 users) (p. 14)
q1_support: p. 4: "A composite channel model including path loss, shadow fading, multipath fading, and inter-beam interference is adopted"; a custom model (Eq. 1) with no 3GPP TR 38.811 profile and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "simulation scenarios set dynamic changes in the number of users (32/64/96/256)"; the paper never states that the trained policy was tested on conditions absent from training, and reports no fine-tuning or transfer result.
q3_support: p. 10: "the original MODRL-TF algorithm [23], the basic PPO algorithm [15], and two traditional non-DRL methods"; compared on throughput, fairness, energy efficiency and other metrics (Figs. 5-10, pp. 11-13).
q4_support: p. 14: "the single inference time of the Attention-MO-PPO algorithm is only 8.7 ms"; the inference order O(N^2) is stated on the same page.
q5_support: p. 10: "The simulation is implemented based on Python 3.9 and PyTorch 2.0 frameworks"; no code or data link is given, and users are placed by random sampling in a custom simulation, so no public dataset is used.
notes: Included, area 6: learned power and frequency-channel allocation for a multi-beam LEO satellite counts as physical layer, and NTN works admit single-antenna links. q2 is 0 because the paper does not state which conditions the policy was trained on; the state and action sizes grow with users K and channels N (p. 7), so the scenario sweeps may be retrained, and the offline fine-tuning loop of p. 7 has no reported result. q1 is 0: ITU-R S.1808-1 is cited only for antenna gain, beamwidth and bandwidth (p. 10), not as a channel model.
